newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer to consider share redemption - CFO.
newsitem.headline: Amer to consider share redemption - CFO.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy will consider using its right to redeem a minority stake in it which was bought by British investor Jonathan Bryan Guinness on Monday, Amer's CFO said on Tuesday.

"The company has the right to redeem the shares. That is undoubtedly one possibility, and we will have to consider what is possible to do and what we want to do," Amer chief financial officer Pekka Paalanne told Reuters by telephone.

Guinness, who is third Lord Moyne, said on Monday he bought 275,000 vote-heavy K shares in Amer, representing 12.5 percent of the votes and 1.2 percent of the shares, for 75 million markka from the Student Union of the Helsinki School of Economics and Business Administration (KY).
The British investor initially bid for an almost 60 percent majority of votes in Amer for 301 million markka but the deal fell through as the three other K shareholders backed out.
Amer now has 30 days to decide whether it will exercise its redemption right to the sold shares. "That gives some sort of deadline (for a decision)," Paalanne said.
"I would imagine that the board will deal with this matter," Paalanne said, but declined to say what the company's further options would be if it chose to buy back the shares.
The three other K shareholders also have a right to redeem the shares bought by Guinness within 60 days.
Paalanne said Amer's business had not yet suffered from the the uncertainty surrounding its ownership following Moyne's bid and its consequent failure.
"(But) it is clear that at some stage it will affect business, and it takes the management's focus away from the normal day-to-day business," Paalannne said.
"It is important from the company's point of view that matters should be made clear," he said.
